nodes.label: Jensen Huang
nodes.relation: Co-founder, CEO and largest individual holder; resigned November 11 and was reinstated November 22, 2026
nodes.summary: Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 11 and the board reinstated him on Nov 22, per NVIDIA's 8-K filings.
brief: Co-founder and chief executive
The founder-CEO's eleven-day exit and return is a governance question for the long.
nodes.health: Holds about 811 million shares directly and through trusts, per his September Form 4.

nodes.label: US Commerce Department (BIS)
nodes.relation: Licenses NVIDIA's chip exports and runs the Section 232 chip tariffs
nodes.summary: Commerce decides which buyers abroad NVIDIA can ship to and is preparing a second round of chip tariffs that may reach servers.
brief: Export licensing and tariff authority
It controls both China access and the tariff bill on servers built for US data centers.
nodes.health: Issued a new remote access rule on November 16 covering five countries.

nodes.label: US Congress
nodes.relation: Writes export control statute and has summoned Huang and Lutnick to testify
nodes.summary: The Senate Banking Committee wants Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick at a public hearing on December 3, while chip export bills were dropped from the defense bill.
brief: Lawmakers overseeing chip exports
A hearing or new statute could harden China limits beyond what the White House allows.
nodes.health: Three chip export bills were cut from the final FY2027 defense bill in November.

nodes.label: Chinese government
nodes.relation: Approves or blocks imports of NVIDIA chips into mainland China
nodes.summary: Beijing has held most licensed H200s outside the mainland to push Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent toward domestic chips.
brief: Gatekeeper for China chip imports
Beijing, not just Washington, now decides whether NVIDIA earns anything in China.
nodes.health: About 600,000 H200s sit in Hong Kong awaiting import approval.

nodes.label: China SAMR
nodes.relation: Antitrust regulator that found NVIDIA broke the conditions on its 2020 Mellanox deal
nodes.summary: SAMR's preliminary finding in September 2025 left a fine of 1% to 10% of prior-year China sales, or remedies, hanging over NVIDIA.
brief: China's market regulator
An open Mellanox case gives Beijing a lever to fine NVIDIA or restrict its networking sales.
nodes.health: Preliminary violation found September 2025; no final penalty announced as of November 2026.

nodes.label: US Justice Department
nodes.relation: Reviewing the $11.9 billion Hugging Face deal inside a wider look at NVIDIA's practices
nodes.summary: The antitrust division is reviewing NVIDIA's deals, including Hugging Face and the Groq licensing arrangement.
brief: US antitrust enforcer
A broad conduct case could limit bundling that keeps NVIDIA's pricing and margins firm.
nodes.health: No second request or lawsuit publicly reported as of late October 2026.

nodes.label: European Commission
nodes.relation: Informal antitrust investigation into NVIDIA's data center business
nodes.summary: The Commission has been asking the industry how to define data center products, the groundwork for a bundling or dominance case.
brief: EU competition authority
An EU case could force NVIDIA to unbundle networking from GPUs in European sales.
nodes.health: Took new steps in its informal NVIDIA probe in October 2026.

nodes.label: Megaspeed
nodes.relation: Singapore cloud buyer of NVIDIA chips suspected of diverting them to China
nodes.summary: Megaspeed bought more than $4 billion of NVIDIA chips, and Treasury wants it blacklisted.
brief: Southeast Asian GPU cloud operator
It is the case Washington is using to tighten sales into Southeast Asia.
nodes.health: Bought over $4 billion of NVIDIA chips; Treasury wants it blacklisted.

nodes.label: Taiwan Strait
nodes.relation: Military risk to TSMC, which makes and packages nearly all NVIDIA chips
nodes.summary: China ran an unannounced, multi-fleet exercise around Taiwan in early November that analysts read as practice for isolating the island.
brief: Geopolitical risk to chip supply
Any blockade would cut the TSMC wafers and CoWoS packaging NVIDIA depends on.
nodes.health: About 100 Chinese ships deployed in early November; no blockade followed.

nodes.label: Vanguard
nodes.relation: Largest institutional holder of NVIDIA common stock
nodes.summary: Vanguard reported 1.78 billion NVIDIA shares, 7.31% of the class, in its Schedule 13G for March 31, 2026.
brief: Largest index fund holder
Passive ownership this large steadies the register but cannot vote out a governance problem.
nodes.health: Owned 7.31% of NVIDIA, 1,777,408,252 shares, at March 31, 2026.

nodes.label: Mark Stevens
nodes.relation: NVIDIA director and one of its largest individual holders
nodes.summary: Stevens sold about $298 million of stock in September at around $220, well above where the shares trade now.
brief: NVIDIA board director
A director selling this much near the top is a read on insider conviction.
nodes.health: Still holds about 27.5 million shares directly and through trusts after the sale.

signals.headline: NVIDIA announces CEO transition as Jensen Huang resigns and Colette Kress becomes interim CEO
signals.whyItMatters: The founder-CEO stepped away for eleven days before the board brought him back on Nov 22, which tested how much of the story rests on one person.
signals.evidence: Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.

signals.headline: US Senate summons Nvidia's Huang and Lutnick to testify
signals.whyItMatters: A public hearing on December 3 keeps NVIDIA's China sales in front of lawmakers who can push for tighter export law.
signals.evidence: requested that they appear in a public hearing on December 3

signals.headline: Nvidia chip restrictions unlikely in final NDAA as GAIN AI and Chip Security Acts are dropped
signals.whyItMatters: Without the GAIN AI Act there is no US-buyers-first rule in statute, so NVIDIA keeps freedom to sell abroad for at least another year.
signals.evidence: Several proposals aimed at AI chip exports were reportedly excluded from the final NDAA negotiations.

signals.headline: NVIDIA stops licensed Hopper shipments to China and guides fourth quarter with no China data center revenue
signals.whyItMatters: China gave NVIDIA $2.4 billion last quarter, about 2% of revenue, and the $130 billion guide already assumes none of it, so the loss is real but already in the numbers.
signals.evidence: Shipments of Data Center Hopper products to China during the quarter were $2.4 billion.

signals.headline: Nvidia H200 chips pile up in Hong Kong as Beijing holds back, Reuters says
signals.whyItMatters: Beijing steering its cloud giants to domestic chips means China demand may not come back even if Washington allows it.
signals.evidence: About 600,000 of Nvidia's H200 AI chips are being stored in Hong Kong.

signals.headline: US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
signals.whyItMatters: Licenses are now needed to ship to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which slows sales to the Southeast Asian clouds that rent compute to Chinese firms.
signals.evidence: Nvidia shares fell 4.1% on Monday and have lost more than 30% of their market value over the past month.

signals.headline: Treasury's Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chips to China
signals.whyItMatters: If Megaspeed is blacklisted, a buyer of more than $4 billion of NVIDIA chips goes away and other Southeast Asian customers face closer checks.
signals.evidence: Megaspeed has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.
signals.sourceName: Associated Press via Anchorage Daily News

signals.headline: Chip Tariff Phase Two confirmed: build in America or pay, Lutnick announces
signals.whyItMatters: If phase two drops the data center exemption and reaches servers, every rack the hyperscalers import gets more expensive and their budgets buy fewer of them.
signals.evidence: Companies that don't manufacture in the US should expect to pay to enter the greatest market in the world.

signals.headline: Applying semiconductor and server tariffs to data centers would now cost the US about $180 billion a year, CCIA says
signals.whyItMatters: A 25% tariff on chips and servers works out to a 15.6% tax on data center construction, which would come straight out of the capex that drives NVIDIA's demand.
signals.evidence: would put about $900 billion of planned 2027 to 2031 U.S. data center investment at risk

signals.headline: US DOJ examines Nvidia's $12.93 billion Hugging Face acquisition
signals.whyItMatters: The review sits inside a broader look at NVIDIA's conduct, including the Groq deal, and a conduct case could limit the bundling that supports its pricing.
signals.evidence: The review sits inside a broader examination of Nvidia's business practices.

signals.headline: European Commission takes new steps in informal Nvidia antitrust investigation
signals.whyItMatters: The EU probe is still informal, but it is moving toward a case that could make NVIDIA sell GPUs and networking separately in Europe.
signals.evidence: European Commission takes new steps in informal Nvidia antitrust investigation

signals.headline: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
signals.whyItMatters: Roughly 100 ships drilled around Taiwan without a blockade, which shows both how exposed TSMC's supply is and that shipping kept moving.
signals.evidence: We are not going to wake up tomorrow to an operation where Taiwan is being taken by force.

signals.headline: Director Mark Stevens sells 1,356,000 NVIDIA shares at an average of $219.72
signals.whyItMatters: A director cashing out about $298 million two months before the shares fell below $150 is a sign insiders saw the stock as fully priced.
signals.evidence: Shares sold: 1,356,000 at a weighted average price of $219.7219

signals.headline: General Counsel Tim Teter sells 30,000 NVIDIA shares between $146 and $157 under a 10b5-1 plan
signals.whyItMatters: The sale is small and was set up in May, so it says little about conviction, but it shows insiders still selling with the stock near $150.
signals.evidence: effected pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted by the Reporting Person on May 22, 2026
